item.title: UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo to visit Jamaica this week
item.description: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Administrator and United Nations (UN) Under-Secretary-General, Alexander De Croo will be visiting Jamaica this week. From March 5 to 6, De Croo is expected to visit Hurricane Melissa-impacted communities and engage in crisis-resilience and hurricane-recovery talks with government and private sector partners. The post UNDP Administrator Alexander De Croo to visit Jamaica this week appeared first on IRIE FM.

item.title: Jamaica recorded largest quarterly economic decline since COVID-19 pandemic in October to December period last year
item.description: There was a 7.5% contraction compared to the corresponding period in 2024.The data was presented by Director General of the Planning Institute of Jamaica (PIOJ), Dr. Wayne Henry, during the PIOJ quarterly review of the economy this morning. The post Jamaica recorded largest quarterly economic decline since COVID-19 pandemic in October to December period last year appeared first on IRIE FM.

item.title: Auditor General’s Department says it’s fairly satisfied with financial management operations at Ministry of Local Government
item.description: Deputy Auditor General, Marlon McAdam, made the disclosure at this morning's sitting of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament.He was giving an overview of an audit conducted of the Ministry's appropriation accounts for the 2023/2024 period. item.title: AuGD says outstanding financial statements to be submitted by Municipal Corporations climbs to 95
item.description: Deputy Auditor General Marlon McAdam is reporting an increase in the number of outstanding financial statements to be submitted by Municipal Corporations (MCs).Mr. McAdam, who was speaking on the Auditor General's 2025 Annual Report, said 95 financial statements were outstanding. item.title: ODPEM to test tsunami early warning system in Port Maria, St. Mary on March 19
item.description: The Office of the Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) will partner with several local stakeholders to test a tsunami early warning system in Port Maria, St Mary, on March 19.The disclosure was made by ODPEM's Regional Coordinator, Marlon Brown, at Monday's meeting of the St. Mary Chamber of Commerce, which was held at the Casa Maria Hotel in Port Maria. The post ODPEM to test tsunami early warning system in Port Maria, St. Mary on March 19 appeared first on IRIE FM.
